module-1-profile-card-project.label: Module Project: Build a Profile Card
module-1-profile-card-project.summary: Build one profile-card program cumulatively: start with stored values, make it interactive, clean typed text, then convert an age and calculate next year's value. Every step begins with the exact previous solution.

mp_4.title: Step 4: Add age conversion and calculation

mp-1-store-profile-values.title: Build the stored-value profile card
mp-1-store-profile-values.prompt:
Upgrade the preview into a two-line profile card. Replace the preview program by storing `"Maya"` in `student_name` and `7` in `level`. Use f-strings to print exactly:

```text
Profile for Maya
Level: 7
```
mp-1-store-profile-values.hint: Replace the preview with the two assignments, then interpolate both variables in labeled f-strings.

help.concept: This step combines variables with basic f-string interpolation.
help.hint_1: Use `student_name` and `level` as the variable names.
help.hint_2: Print two lines: the profile label first and the level label second.

0.message: Store Maya in student_name and 7 in level, then use both variables in the two f-string output lines.

mp-2-read-and-label-input.title: Make the profile card interactive
mp-2-read-and-label-input.prompt:
Keep the working card structure. Replace the stored name with the first `input()`, keep `level = 7`, read a city with a second `input()`, and add the city line. Print exactly:

```text
Profile for <name>
Level: 7
City: <city>
```
mp-2-read-and-label-input.hint: Change only what the new requirement needs: name becomes input, city is added as input, and the existing level line stays.

help.concept: The same formatted card now uses runtime text values supplied by the learner.
help.hint_1: The input order is name, then city.
help.hint_2: Preserve the two existing output lines and add `City:` as the third line.

mp-2-read-and-label-input.solutionCode:
student_name = input()
level = 7
city = input()
print(f"Profile for {student_name}")
print(f"Level: {level}")
print(f"City: {city}")

0.message: Read the name and city with two input() calls.

1.message: Keep the profile, level, and city output in that order.

mp-3-clean-typed-name.title: Clean the typed profile text
mp-3-clean-typed-name.prompt: Keep the same three-line card and the same input order. Clean outside whitespace from both the typed name and typed city with `.strip()` before printing them.
mp-3-clean-typed-name.hint: Apply `.strip()` to the string returned by each text input.

help.concept: This step improves the same interactive card using the string-cleanup method already learned.
help.hint_1: The name can be read as `input().strip()`.
help.hint_2: Do the same for the city; keep `level = 7` unchanged.

mp-3-clean-typed-name.starterCode:
student_name = input()
level = 7
city = input()
print(f"Profile for {student_name}")
print(f"Level: {level}")
print(f"City: {city}")
mp-3-clean-typed-name.solutionCode:
student_name = input().strip()
level = 7
city = input().strip()
print(f"Profile for {student_name}")
print(f"Level: {level}")
print(f"City: {city}")

0.message: Use .strip() on both typed text values.

1.message: Keep the existing three-line card structure.

mp-4-build-full-profile-card.title: Finish the interactive profile card
mp-4-build-full-profile-card.prompt:
Keep the cleaned name and city. Replace `level = 7` with a typed age from the second input line, convert it with `int()`, and change the middle output line to next year's age.

The input order is name, age, city. Print exactly:

```text
Profile for <clean name>
Age next year: <age + 1>
City: <clean city>
```
mp-4-build-full-profile-card.hint: Preserve the cleaned text logic, convert only the age, and use `age + 1` inside the middle f-string.

help.concept: The final step combines input, string cleanup, integer conversion, arithmetic, variables, and f-string output in one cumulative program.
help.hint_1: The second input must become an integer before you add 1.
help.hint_2: Do not remove the `.strip()` calls already working for the name and city.

mp-4-build-full-profile-card.starterCode:
student_name = input().strip()
level = 7
city = input().strip()
print(f"Profile for {student_name}")
print(f"Level: {level}")
print(f"City: {city}")
mp-4-build-full-profile-card.solutionCode:
student_name = input().strip()
age = int(input())
city = input().strip()
print(f"Profile for {student_name}")
print(f"Age next year: {age + 1}")
print(f"City: {city}")

1.message: Convert the age with int() before calculating age + 1.

2.message: Use f-strings to print the three labeled profile lines.
